meta.title: mph to m/s — Convert Mile/hour to Meter/second | Turbo Unit
meta.description: Convert Mile/hour (mph) to Meter/second (m/s) instantly. 1 mph = 0.44704 m/s. Free, accurate, engineering-grade precision.

content.intro: Convert mile/hours (mph) to meter/seconds (m/s) instantly. Both measure speed, so the relationship is strictly linear: each mile/hour equals 0.44704 meter/seconds. Use the converter above for any value, or read on for the formula, a quick lookup table, and practical tips.
content.result_section: One mile/hour is equal to **0.44704 meter/seconds**. To go the other way, one meter/second equals **2.2369363 mile/hours**. For everyday use, rounding to 2–4 decimal places is usually enough; for engineering or scientific work, keep the full precision shown by the converter.
content.formula_section:
The conversion is a single multiplication:

> meter/seconds = mile/hours × 0.44704

Worked example — converting 10 mile/hours:

10 × 0.44704 = **4.4704 m/s**.

To invert, divide by 0.44704 (or multiply by 2.2369363).

- Travel planning where signage and maps use different unit systems.
- DIY and home-improvement projects that mix metric materials with imperial tools.
- Fitness tracking when devices report in one system and goals are set in another.
- Shipping and logistics where weight and dimensions drive cost.
content.tips:
Keep the factor handy: 1 mph ≈ 0.44704 m/s. For rough mental math, round to the nearest sensible digit.

Mind the units. Mile/hour and Meter/second both measure speed; squared or cubic variants need a different factor (factor², factor³).

When precision matters (engineering, lab work, dosing), avoid rounding mid-calculation — convert once at the final step using the full factor.
content.faq:
**Q:** How many meter/seconds are in 1 mile/hour?
**A:** 0.44704 meter/seconds.

**Q:** What's the formula to convert mph to m/s?
**A:** meter/seconds = mile/hours × 0.44704.

**Q:** How do I convert m/s back to mph?
**A:** Multiply by 2.2369363 (or divide by 0.44704).

**Q:** Is rounding to 2 decimal places accurate enough?
**A:** For most everyday uses, yes. For scientific or engineering work, use the full precision from the converter.

**Q:** Does this mph to m/s converter work offline?
**A:** Yes — all math runs in your browser, no network required after the page loads.
